bio: What began as a popular stall in Brooklyn’s DeKalb Market Hall has grown into this lively Ridgewood restaurant and market, where they offer a contemporary take on Polish comfort food. Pierogi remain the main attraction, especially the classic “Ruskie” version filled with potato and cheese and topped with caramelized onions, sour cream and chives. Elsewhere, the kitchen shows a lighter touch with dishes like Berkshire pork schnitzel paired with endive and dill pickle dressing, as well as potato pancakes topped with smoked trout rillette and horseradish cream. A playful cocktail list, including pickle martinis, adds to the appeal.
